Anchor resolution moved out of the build loop first, in its own commit with no change to built sites, so a draft can resolve against the same context per request.

Chose: Prompts and annotations follow their entry, not their exact place in it

where src/render.ts file page

quote ${plan.entries.map((e) => entryHtml(here, plan, e) + extras(e.slug)).join('\n')}

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan placed annotations after the entry holding their quote; prompts get the same treatment. A prompt is taken out of its entry's markdown and shown after the entry's reason, which is where a draft's prompts sit anyway. A note with no quote, or whose quote is gone, comes first.

Chose: Notes count as current when they match annotations.nvim's own hash

where src/draft.ts file page

quote const current = !!annotates && [source, source.replace(/\n$/, '')].some((v) => sha256(v).startsWith(annotates));

Because (measured): the plan said the page shows the notes' hash, so an annotation can say which version it answered. The notes file already says which version of the draft it annotates, annotates: plan.draft.md sha256:…, so the page compares that instead and says when the draft has moved since. annotations.nvim hashes the buffer's lines joined by newlines (its sha_of), which drops the file's final newline; hashing the file as-is would have called every note out of date.

Chose: A restated prompt in the notes is its answer, matched by kind and exact text

where src/draft.ts file page

quote const prompt = restated && all.find((p) => p.kind.toLowerCase() === restated[1].toLowerCase() && p.text === restated[2].trim());

Because (Claude, not asked): the agreement says an answer restates the question so the notes stand alone. Restating it exactly is what annotations.nvim does; a restated heading that matches no prompt is shown as an ordinary annotation, not dropped.

Chose: The draft link is added by the server, not built into pages

where src/serve.ts file page

quote function withDraftLink(html: string, here: string): string {

Because (Claude, not asked): built pages are a function of the commit and can't know about a working-tree file, so the dev server adds rel="draft" to each page's header as it serves it, while the draft exists. A built site is unchanged.

Chose: A draft reads the site's places but isn't listed on them

where src/site.ts file page

quote ra.place = cx.places.get(placeKey(t));

Because (Claude, not asked): the plan said a built site never contains a draft; the place pages are built once, so a draft can't appear on them without rebuilding. Its anchors link a place page when the site has one, and other plans' entries don't list it under "anchored by."
